result:
The services now talk through an event bus instead of calling each other directly. The full suite passes (`python -m pytest -q`: 31 passed), and each test file also passes when run on its own. All the existing tests pass without changes.

**New code**
- `src/core/events.py` has `EventBus` with `subscribe` and `publish`, plus the module-level `event_bus`. Handlers run synchronously in the order they subscribed, and errors reach the caller just as they did before. I also added an `unsubscribe` you didn't ask for, and subscribing the same handler twice has no effect.

**Service changes**
- **Billing and subscription:** neither imports `audit_service` any more. They publish `subscription.created`, `payment.processed`, `subscription.cancelled`, `subscription.upgraded` and `subscription.paused`, each carrying the same actor, target and changes the old audit call used.
- **Audit:** `audit_service` subscribes to those five events plus `webhook.processed` and calls `record(...)` with the same arguments, so the audit entries are identical.
- **Webhook:** `webhook_service` no longer imports billing, subscription or audit. It publishes `webhook.<stripe event type>` (for example `webhook.invoice.payment_succeeded`) and then `webhook.processed`.

**Two things that work differently from what you might assume**
- **The webhook handlers moved, and only telemetry was there to move.** The old webhook handlers only bumped telemetry counters; they never actually called billing or subscription. I moved those counters into subscriber methods on `billing_service` (payment succeeded/failed) and `subscription_service` (subscription deleted/updated), so the end result is the same.
- **The bus is wired up when the services package loads.** `src/services/__init__.py` now imports all four services so their subscriptions are always registered. Without it, code that imported only `billing_service` would publish to an audit service that never subscribed, and no audit entries would be written.

`tests/test_events.py` adds 8 tests:
- the bus itself: subscriber order, events with no subscribers, matching by event name, unsubscribing, and errors reaching the caller;
- checks that billing, subscription and webhook calls produce exactly the expected audit entries through the bus;
- a check that the webhook's payment counter still increments.

I did this directly in this session instead of handing it to sub-agents, because it touched every service at once. Nothing is committed. A `.godmode/` folder appeared in the working tree and is untracked; you may want to add it to `.gitignore`.
